# Registering an encrypted Amazon S3 location with Lake Formation

## Before you begin

You need the following in place before you start:

- An existing KMS-encrypted S3 bucket or location in the other AWS account (account B) that you want to register. This is the location you will register in the final step.
- A customer managed KMS key used to encrypt that S3 location. You will need it for the key policy step, in which you edit the key policy in AWS KMS.

## Encryption support and bucket considerations

Lake Formation integrates with AWS KMS to let integrated services encrypt and decrypt data in Amazon S3 locations. Both customer managed keys and AWS managed keys are supported. Client-side encryption/decryption is not supported.

Avoid registering an Amazon S3 bucket that has Requester pays enabled. For buckets registered with Lake Formation, the role used to register the bucket is always viewed as the requester. The bucket owner is charged for data access when another AWS account accesses the bucket. That charge arrangement holds only when the role used to register the bucket belongs to the same account as the bucket owner.

## The cross-account scenario

This procedure covers registering an AWS KMS-encrypted S3 bucket in account B using an IAM role in account A. Because you are doing this, the role in account A must grant permissions on the bucket in account B, and the bucket policy in account B must grant access permissions to the role in account A. The KMS key is in account B. Because the registration is cross-account and the key is in account B, the key policy must grant access to the role in account A, and the role in account A must grant permissions on the KMS key. Neither of these two key permissions applies unless both conditions hold: you are registering the bucket in account B using the role in account A, and the KMS key is in account B.

Lake Formation assumes the registered role when accessing underlying data in Amazon S3, and the assumed role has the required permissions on the KMS key. For that reason, you don't have to grant KMS key permissions to principals accessing underlying data with ETL jobs or integrated services such as Amazon Athena.

## Step 1: Use a user-defined role

You can't use the Lake Formation service-linked role to register a location in another account. You must use a user-defined role to register a cross-account location. Using a user-defined role means it must meet the requirements for roles used to register locations. In particular, the role must include a policy that grants Amazon S3 permissions on the location. Create or update this role, with that policy, before you register the location, because the role you choose at registration is the role from this step.

## Step 2: Add the key and bucket permissions

If the KMS key is not in the same account as the Data Catalog, an inline policy granting the required KMS key permissions must be added to the role. This inline policy applies only when the KMS key is not in the same account as the Data Catalog.

Next, add a bucket policy granting the required S3 permissions to the role on the Amazon S3 console.

Then, in AWS KMS, add the role as a user of the KMS key. Adding the role as a user of the key is enough to result in the ARN of the role being added to the Allow use of the key object in the key policy. If the Allow use of the key object is missing from the key policy, you must add it with the permissions shown in the example. Adding it with those permissions applies only when the object is missing.

Complete both the bucket policy and the KMS key user step before you move on to registration.

## Step 3: Register the location

Only after the bucket policy is added and the role is added as a user of the KMS key, the user registering the location signs into the Data Catalog account as the data lake administrator.

When registering, type the S3 path manually in the format `s3://<bucket>/<prefix>`. Cross-account buckets do not appear in the list when you choose Browse. For the role, choose the role from Step 2.

# Lake Formation and AWS KMS encryption

Lake Formation integrates with AWS KMS so that integrated services can encrypt and decrypt data in Amazon S3 locations. Both customer managed keys and AWS managed keys are supported. Client-side encryption and decryption is not supported.

## Requester pays buckets

Avoid registering an Amazon S3 bucket that has Requester pays enabled. For buckets registered with Lake Formation, the role used to register the bucket is always viewed as the requester. The bucket owner is charged for data access when another AWS account accesses the bucket. The role used to register the bucket belongs to the same account as the bucket owner.

## Accessing encrypted data

Lake Formation assumes the registered role when it accesses underlying data in Amazon S3. Because the assumed role has the required permissions on the KMS key, you don't have to grant KMS key permissions to principals that access the underlying data with ETL jobs or integrated services such as Amazon Athena.

## Registering a cross-account, KMS-encrypted bucket

This scenario registers an AWS KMS-encrypted S3 bucket in account B using an IAM role in account A. You can't use the Lake Formation service-linked role to register a location in another account. You must use a user-defined role, and that role must meet the requirements for roles used to register locations, including a policy that grants Amazon S3 permissions on the location.

The following permissions must be in place:

- The role in account A must grant permissions on the bucket in account B.
- The bucket policy in account B must grant access permissions to the role in account A.
- The KMS key is in account B, so the key policy must grant access to the role in account A.
- The role in account A must grant permissions on the KMS key.

Because the KMS key is not in the same account as the Data Catalog, you must take these steps:

1. Add an inline policy granting the required KMS key permissions to the role.
2. On the Amazon S3 console, add a bucket policy granting the required S3 permissions to the role.
3. In AWS KMS, add the role as a user of the KMS key. To do this, add the ARN of the role to the Allow use of the key object in the key policy. If the Allow use of the key object is missing from the key policy, add it with the permissions shown in the example.

## Completing the registration

The user registering the location signs into the Data Catalog account as the data lake administrator. Cross-account buckets do not appear in the list when you choose Browse, so you must type the S3 path manually in the format `s3://<bucket>/<prefix>`. The role you choose for registration is the role from Step 2.

Avoid registering an Amazon S3 bucket that has Requester pays enabled. For buckets registered with Lake Formation, the role used to register the bucket is always viewed as the requester. The bucket owner is charged for data access when another AWS account accesses the bucket. The scenario here is registering an AWS KMS-encrypted S3 bucket in account B using an IAM role in account A. The role in account A must grant permissions on the bucket in account B, and the bucket policy in account B must grant access permissions to the role in account A.

The KMS key is in account B. Because the registration is being done and the key is in account B, the key policy must grant access to the role in account A, and the role in account A must grant permissions on the KMS key.
